title: Migration Bridge for Regulated POCs — Guide
body:
Purpose:
This note captures a minimal, repeatable 'migration bridge' pattern to move a regulated-data POC from (A) an initial hosted proof-of-concept into (B) dedicated capacity and optionally (C) a private/VPC on-prem deployment. The goal is to document a low-friction, auditable sequence that SRE, SE, and Security can run with customers who must demonstrate data residency, minimal data egress, and KMS/HSM integration during a short pilot (4–8 weeks).

Scope and assumptions:
- Customer requires that sensitive data never be stored outside customer-controlled storage during phase 2/3.
- Initial POC (phase 0–1) runs on Redwood hosted API for speed.
- Customer will progress to dedicated capacity for throughput predictability, then optionally switch to private deployment for final compliance.
- Expected stakeholders: SE (lead), SRE (capacity/canary), Security (KMS & audit), Customer infra (network peering/VPN), PM/CS.

Decision criteria (quick checklist):
- Compliance: is certified on-prem mandatory, or is VPC-enforced private control plane sufficient? (owner: Security)
- Latency: 50–150ms SLOs? If <50ms, consider on-prem edge. (owner: SE)
- Throughput: bursty vs steady QPS (owner: SRE + SE)
- Data residency: egress allowed for telemetry/metrics? Define minimal telemetry footprint. (owner: Security + Customer)
- Cost profile: acceptable monthly committed spend for Dedicated vs one-time private setup. (owner: FinOps)

Recommended migration bridge pattern (phases):
Phase A — Pilot (hosted) — 0–2 weeks
- Objective: validate model, prompts, and output quality; collect prompt sets and failure cases.
- Actions: use hosted API keys, enable debug logging for prompt-response pairs but redact PII, set retention TTL appropriate to compliance.
- Deliverable: validated test prompts, initial SLO targets, runbook skeleton.

Phase B — Bridge (dedicated reserved capacity) — 1–3 weeks
- Objective: reproduce pilot performance on customer-bound capacity with isolated GPU pools and defined routing policies.
- Actions: allocate dedicated pool (min nodes), configure autoscale floor, configure tenant slice (if multi-tenant), enable prefix caching for repeated-latency-sensitive queries.
- Security: integrate customer KMS for key wrapping where required; configure VPC peering if customer requests private egress path.
- Telemetry: mirror metrics to customer SIEM/observability; reduce hosted retention.
- Deliverable: dedicated endpoint with SLA template, capacity runbook, and cost estimate.

Phase C — Private (VPC / on-prem) — 2–4 weeks (optional)
- Objective: full compliance posture, integrate with customer's KMS/HSM, audit logs forwarded to customer SIEM, optional air-gapped deployment.
- Actions: prepare minimal config snapshot from dedicated stage, coordinate network setup (VPN/Direct Connect), deploy private control plane and inference nodes behind customer network, validate inference kernel compatibility and quantization settings in target hardware.
- Deliverable: private deployment checklist, acceptance test results, compliance sign-off.

Canary and fallbacks (common pattern):
- Canary sequence: 1) 1% traffic to dedicated endpoint, 2) 5% after 24h if no regressions, 3) 25% with load tests, 4) 100% after 72h. Each step gated by quality metrics (latency, 99th percentile, exact-match regression rate on eval set).
- Fallbacks: route to hosted-compatible model variant if resource pressure or model regression detected. Keep a cached prefix on hosted for last-resort low-latency responses.

Key technical checklist (engineers):
- Model packaging: ensure deterministic model hash and reproducible init. Track model version in deployment manifests.
- KV cache warm-up script and priming prompts.
- Tokenization parity tests between hosted and private runtime.
- Quantization profile verification (8-bit vs 4-bit) and accuracy baseline.
- Autoscaling profile: CPU/GPU thresholds, queue depth limits, max token concurrency.
- Request routing policy: region/latency/cost priority matrix.

Security & compliance knobs:
- KMS: key-wrapping for model artifacts and customer data; document KMS policies.
- Audit logs: full request metadata (exclude PII). Forward logs to customer SIEM with signed delivery.
- Network controls: allowlist only customer CIDRs, enforce mTLS for control plane.
- Data residency: set retention TTLs at phase boundaries, document data-at-rest and in-transit encryption.

Observability & SLOs:
- Latency SLOs: p95 and p99 targets per route.
- Quality SLOs: hallucination/regression checks on canonical prompt suite (daily).
- Cost SLO: per-token and per-embedding spend target with alerting when overruns >10%.
- Dashboard minimums: per-route token breakdown, model-level 99th percentile latency, cache hit-rate, top failing prompts.

Runbook (quick play):
- Deploy: update manifest, kick canary at 1% traffic, run smoke tests (latency < target, responses within quality thresholds).
- Monitor: watch p50/p95/p99, error rate, cache hit-rate, memory pressure.
- Escalate: on regression, revert route to previous model, mark incident in tracker (JIRA POC-9123), notify CS and customer infra.

Timeline and rough effort estimate (for a typical mid-size regulated customer):
- Hosted pilot: 1–2 weeks (SE + customer devs)
- Dedicated bridge: 1–3 weeks (SRE + infra + SE)
- Private deployment (optional): 2–6 weeks (security, customer infra coordination)

Open questions / risks (to resolve before kickoff):
- Telemetry: exactly which telemetry fields can be forwarded to Redwood hosted systems? (owner: Security)
- KMS SLA: can customer provide HSM-backed keys in time for dedicated stage? (owner: Customer infra)
- Network egress cost policy: who pays for cross-region traffic during bridge period? (owner: FinOps)
- Acceptance criteria: what is the minimum eval pass rate to move from dedicated to private? (owner: PM + Customer)

Next steps (immediate):
- Align on decision criteria doc with customer (share by EOD).
- Create dedicated pool estimate and draft commitment ask.
- Schedule a 60-min workshop (SE + SRE + Security + customer infra) to map out test prompts and telemetry acceptance.

Notes to self / workshop prompts:
- Bring small set of canonical prompts that break easily (for regression detection).
- Prepare network checklist sample for customer: peering, route tables, firewall ports, NAT egress rules.
- Keep cost model simple: per-token + committed node hours; outline delta for private one-time setup.

Captured artifacts to attach to final playbook: pilot results CSV, canary metric snapshot, minimal network diagram, KMS integration checklist.

----
Informal: this doc is intentionally compact — we should expand into a slide one-pager for CS and a formal runbook template for SRE after the workshop. Also want to validate if the customer accepts minor telemetry exported (metrics only) or absolutely zero telemetry to hosted telemetry backends (makes observability much harder).
